long_biography.plain_text:
Education became Alberto Baillères González's most sustained public institution beyond business. An economics graduate of ITAM, he chaired its governing board from 1967 and helped develop the school into one of Latin America's leading universities while preserving its academic autonomy. He also led the Mexican Cultural Association, which supports the institute.

Mexico's Senate awarded Baillères the Belisario Domínguez Medal in 2015, recognising his contribution to economic, educational and cultural development. He also backed health and literary organisations, but ITAM remained the clearest expression of his long institutional stewardship. He continued chairing its governing board after handing Grupo BAL's presidency to his son Alejandro.
